Brand guide and design kit

The reference to approve before building the app: identity, tokens, components, 46 screens, flows and business rules taken from the 8 mockup boards.

Mobile iOS / AndroidWebEnglish by default, French optionalVersion 1.0 · October 2026

Principles

Keeplas keeps what matters for later. The interface must reassure without dramatising: calm, readable, explicit about who can see what and when.

Calm firstNight blue, ivory, landscapes at dawn. Never red except to revoke, reject or alert.
Always say who sees whatEvery sharing screen shows scope, timing and permission. Trust contacts cannot read files, and we keep saying it.
One action per screenA single primary button. The life check has one button and no snooze.
Security is visible'Encrypted on your device' banners, securing states, device alerts: protection is shown, not hidden.
English by defaultThe app opens in English. French is optional; every string exists in both languages. Allow 20% more length for French.
No email, no passwordVerified phone + passkey. The number identifies, it never unlocks.

Logo

A shield carrying a ring and a keyhole: protection and transmission. The wordmark is set in Source Serif 4 SemiBold.

Clear space: the height of the ring on every side. Minimum symbol size: 20 px (16 px favicon: solid shield only). Do not distort, do not recolour outside navy-900 / white, do not place on a busy photo. App icon: white symbol on navy-900, native iOS radius.

Business rules

What the mockups promise the user. The code must keep every one of these promises.

Platforms and sign-up

  • Sign-up happens only in the mobile app (iOS / Android). The web app has no sign-up form.
  • On desktop, a visitor without an account is invited to download the app: store badges and a QR code that opens the right store.
  • A computer is only connected by scanning a QR code from the phone app; later visits on a trusted browser use a passkey.
  • Invitations opened on a computer also lead to the app: contacts and beneficiaries sign up on their phone.
  • Setup, the 24-word kit and every recovery path run on the phone; the web Recovery center only shows status.

Language

  • English is the app's default language, on mobile and web, including on first launch.
  • French is offered through the language selector; the choice is saved on the account and the device.
  • Any key missing in French falls back to English.

Identity

  • The account is identified by a phone number verified with a WhatsApp code. No email is required.
  • The number is used to find the account. It is never enough to unlock the vault.
  • WhatsApp is only used for notifications: no vault content goes through it.

Authentication

  • Sign-in with a device-bound passkey (Face ID or fingerprint), no password.
  • Optional 6-digit Keeplas code, asked after biometrics when enabled.
  • On the web: the first sign-in is always a QR link from the phone (expires after about 2 minutes); later sign-ins on a trusted browser use a passkey. No password, no phrase entry on the web.

Vault and encryption

  • The vault is created and encrypted on the device. Keeplas cannot read its content.
  • Each captured item is encrypted before leaving the device, then uploaded and marked Protected.
  • Categories: Documents, Accounts, Instructions, Other, plus the Encrypted inbox (items to sort).

Setup

  • Required (3): verify the number, create a passkey, create the vault.
  • Optional (2): add trust contacts, export a 24-word recovery kit.
  • Without contacts or a kit, losing every device and passkey can lock the user out for good: say it clearly.

Trust contacts and beneficiaries

  • Up to 3 trust contacts; 2 confirmations are enough.
  • Trust contact: helps recover access and confirms a death. Cannot read files.
  • Beneficiary: receives the content assigned to them, now or later.
  • The two roles are independent and can be combined. Replacing a contact renews protection.

Access recovery

  • 3 methods: another signed-in device, trust contacts, recovery kit.
  • Through contacts: 2 approvals + a 48 h protection window starting at the request.
  • A 4-digit code is compared by phone or video call between the owner and each contact.
  • The owner can cancel during the window. At the end: new passkey, protection renewed, data still encrypted.

Succession

  • 2 trust contacts confirm the death, then a 72 h grace period applies.
  • Only assigned content is released, folder by folder.
  • Sharing timing per folder: now, or after verification and waiting period.

Life check

  • Periodic check with a single action and no snooze.
  • A missed answer never triggers sharing on its own. Keeplas checks again later before any other step.

Sharing

  • Scope: this folder only. The recipient sees nothing else in the vault.
  • View permission: view and download.
  • Revoking prevents future access, but copies already saved cannot be removed.

Devices

  • Linking a browser requires Face ID on the phone.
  • Every device is notified of each new link or sign-in.
  • New device alert: It was me / It wasn't me. Any device can be revoked.
  • Optional encrypted backups: Keeplas, iCloud, Google.

Open decisions

Inconsistencies and gaps found in the mockups. Settle them before the first sprint.

  1. Mobile-only sign-up (decided)Sign-up only in the iOS / Android app; the computer is linked by QR. To do: design the desktop 'Get the Keeplas app' screen (store badges, QR to the store, 'I already have the app → Link with my phone'), drop W05-1 / W05-2 from scope, and remove web sign-up from the repo (finding F8).
  2. Shamir thresholdThe PRD says Shamir 3-of-5. The code splits into 4 shares (1 on the device, 3 for contacts) with threshold 2 or 3; the designs show 3 contacts, any 2 enough. See findings F1 and F2 in Security, then align the PRD.
  3. 48 h or 72 hRecovery: 48 h protection window. Succession: 72 h grace period. Confirm this is intended and keep these two names everywhere.
  4. Mobile navigationIn French, 'Personnes' on some boards and 'Contacts' on others. Pick one label.
  5. Web navigationThree different sidebars across boards. Proposal: My vault, Shared with me, People, Life check, Devices, Settings, plus Recovery center reachable from Settings.
  6. Life check nameIn French, 'Vie continue' and 'vérification de vie' coexist. Pick one term.
  7. Language selectorEnglish by default is decided. The selector still needs unifying: EN | FR segment, dropdown and 'Language' row coexist. Proposal: compact dropdown in the header, row in Settings. Several FR mockups show FR preselected: in production, EN is preselected until the user chooses.
  8. Life-check frequencyFrequency, number of reminders and what happens after a long silence are not defined in the designs (the repo uses weekly / monthly / quarterly).
  9. Optional backupsAll 3 toggles are on in the mockup. Decide the default state.
  10. Declining an invitationThe invitation screen has no Decline action.
  11. Brands and photosThe mockups use the Chrome logo and portraits. The kit uses a generic browser icon and initials avatars; plan licensed visuals if needed.
  12. Undesigned statesOTP error, passkey failure, camera denied, offline, upload failure, expired invitation, rejected request, empty states, 'It wasn't me' flow.
  13. Dark mode and tabletNot designed. Tokens are ready for a dark theme but values remain to be defined.
